title: The AI-Native Software Engineer | Addy Osmani
summary: Addy Osmani: AI-native engineering, context engineering, the review bottleneck, the 70% problem, and protecting junior skills.

assertions.quote: every engineer is going to evolve from a pure implementer to an orchestrator of agents

verdicts.note: Background and parallel agents are increasingly used, but most developers still work interactively with one agent; enterprise adoption of orchestration is early.
The review documents a role shift toward supervising and validating AI output. Multi-agent orchestration specifically is barely studied.
Anthropic interviews: many engineers describe moving from writing code to managing AIs, some constantly running several Claude instances; self-reported by early adopters at an AI lab.

assertions.quote: Context is king in this moment

verdicts.note: As models improved, output depends more on relevant, high-signal context than phrasing; consistent with Anthropic/Cursor guidance and long-context degradation evidence.

assertions.quote: planning before you prompt and it's providing that clear context

verdicts.note: Clear requirements, examples and references reliably improve agent output; the caveat is that bloated context can hurt, so curation matters.

assertions.quote: never commit code that you can't explain to other people, or even to yourself

verdicts.note: Ownership and maintainability require understanding; it's a reasonable review standard rather than an empirical finding.

assertions.quote: AI is a multiplier. So, what helps the human can help the AI. So, invest in tests, CI, clear documentation

verdicts.note: DORA 2025 found AI amplifies existing engineering practices; strong fundamentals predict AI benefit.

assertions.quote: usage is high. It continues to go up but trust is sliding

verdicts.note: Stack Overflow surveys show trust in AI accuracy fell from about 40% (2024) to about 30% (2025) while usage rose.

assertions.quote: PR sizes have exploded anywhere up to 154%

verdicts.note: The SmartBear/Cisco review study found defect detection drops beyond ~200-400 LOC per session; AI makes large PRs cheap to produce.
The vibe-coding review names a verification gap between generation speed and developers' capacity to verify. It doesn't measure PR size.

Authors note Claude made 3,957 commits and ~500K added lines in Anthropic's claudes-c-compiler within weeks and infer it is unlikely all of it got thorough human review; an argument from volume, not a measurement of review effectiveness.

Google splits AI migration changes into small sharded changelists per code owner and caps weekly volume to avoid overwhelming reviewers, which implies very large AI changes are not reviewable as-is, though it never measures review quality.

assertions.quote: This is soaking up a lot of those individual gains ... The system moves at the speed of the slowest step

verdicts.note: DORA 2024/25 and Faros 2025 found individual output up while organizational delivery metrics stayed flat or worsened; review and integration become the bottleneck.

assertions.quote: AI can get you about 70% of the way ... that last 30% ... is the hardest part

verdicts.note: Widely observed and consistent with Stanford's rework data and METR; the exact 70/30 split is a heuristic.

METR 2025 preliminary evidence: autonomous Claude 3.7 agents often implement the core functionality of study issues but fail full requirements (docs, lint/style, key tests). This fits 'most of the way'; the paper does not show that the rest stays hard.
Airbnb: 75% done in 4 hours and 97% after 4 days of tuning, with the last 3% needing manual work; but the AI baselines made that residual only about a week of effort, so the tail was not that hard.

assertions.quote: Our first priority is really mitigating skill erosion

verdicts.note: Anthropic's 2026 RCT found AI-assisted learners scored lower on mastery of a new library, and other studies show reduced engagement; effects depend on how AI is used.
The review describes 'cognitive debt': deferring understanding during fast iteration raises later debugging and maintenance costs. It does not measure skill loss directly.

assertions.quote: make sure that we don't inadvertently dry up our talent pipeline

verdicts.note: A straightforward pipeline argument made by IBM and others; the long-run effect is unmeasured yet but well reasoned.

assertions.quote: AI shines in low context situations ... Where it struggles right now is high context novel problems

verdicts.note: Benchmarks and field studies show strong performance on well-specified, common tasks and weaker results on context-heavy, novel logic.

assertions.quote: VIP coding is a gift for prototyping

verdicts.note: Validating demand before building is long-standing product practice; AI lowers prototype cost, making it more attractive.

assertions.quote: a learnings markdown file ... a powerful self-improving cycle

verdicts.note: Encoding lessons in rules and workflows does reduce repeat mistakes, but rule files bloat and conflict if not pruned; gains are real but not automatically compounding.
